operations.description: After the labeling pulse, chase the cells with uridine to obtain an aged population of the previously labeled RNA. RNA turnover during the interval changes how much labeled RNA remains.
operations.mechanism: Uridine chase after metabolic labeling; the readout follows persistence of previously labeled RNA, rather than replacement of bromouridine residues within those same molecules.
operations.information_effect: The aged cohort supports relative RNA stability assessment. The primary source scores stability relative to paired nascent RNA; an immediate pulse sample instead reports RNA synthesis. Chased abundance alone does not establish a synthesis rate.

If doing a chase, after the 30 min incubation, rinse plate twice with PBS, then add back saved media containing 20 mM uridine and incubate for desired time period (6 h may be an appropriate time to start with).
In BruChase-Seq, cells are chased in uridine for different periods of time following Bru-labeling, allowing for the isolation of RNA populations of specific ages.
Score relative stability by ranking the ratio of the RPKM of features obtained from aged RNA samples over paired nascent RNA samples.

evidence.rationale: The primary describes isolation of RNA populations of specific ages after uridine chase, and scores relative stability by aged-versus-nascent RNA representation. This supports persistence and turnover of the original labeled RNA cohort as the chase interpretation; chemical replacement of the label on surviving molecules is not asserted.
